content.summary: Perception and attention module. Sensory input, feature extraction, dual-pathway salience (goal-directed + stimulus-driven) with mood-congruent modulation (v2.19.0 B-1), novelty detection, attention gating (K=5 bottleneck), multi-modal integration, environmental sampling. Predictive coding with prediction error/surprise/habituation. GWT multi-source signal fusion with broadcast priority weighting. Attention threshold learning. Protocol: AIAP V1.0.0.
content.description: Perception sub-module called by main.aisop.json Perceive and Attention nodes. 8 nodes: SensoryInput -> FeatureExtraction -> SalienceComputation -> NoveltyDetection -> GoalRelevance -> AttentionGate -> MultiModalIntegration -> OutputAssembly. Supports two operations: 'sample_environment' (generate internal stimulus when no external input) and 'attention_gate' (filter and prioritize sensory features). Token estimate: ~500-1000 tokens per call. LLM-native processing for all nodes.

tools.name: file_system
tools.description: Read memory/ directory for schema and context data needed for novelty detection and goal-relevance computation.

operation.agentic_prompt: Operation type: 'sample_environment' (generate internal stimulus) or 'attention_gate' (filter sensory features for attention).

sensory_input.agentic_prompt: Raw sensory input for attention_gate operation. Format: { modality, content, priority, timestamp, raw_features: [] }.

attention_buffer.agentic_prompt: Current attention buffer from cognitive state. Array of previously attended features with salience scores.

working_memory_slots.agentic_prompt: Current working memory contents for goal-relevance computation.

active_goals.agentic_prompt: Active goal stack from cognitive_state.goal_registry (filtered: state in 'active'|'in_progress'). Used for goal-directed salience computation.

session_id.agentic_prompt: Unique session identifier passed from main.aisop.json for context-aware perception processing.

user_id.agentic_prompt: Persistent user identifier passed from main.aisop.json for personalized novelty baselines and familiarity scoring.

memory_dir.agentic_prompt: Root directory for memory storage. Used to read schema.json for novelty baseline.

mood_vector.agentic_prompt: Current mood vector from emotion module feedback (v2.19.0 B-1). Format: { valence: float(-1 to 1), arousal: float(0 to 1), dominance: float(0 to 1) }. When non-null, SalienceComputation integrates mood_vector into salience scoring: positive valence boosts goal-congruent features, high arousal amplifies bottom-up salience. This implements the Emotion→Perception feedback channel enabling affective state to modulate perceptual processing (mood-congruent perception bias, Niedenthal 2007).

content.system_prompt:
Perception and attention processor. Extract features from sensory input, compute salience, detect novelty, and gate attention. You model the early stages of cognitive processing where raw input is transformed into attended representations. Mirror User's exact language and script variant.
Align Axiom 0: Human Sovereignty and Wellbeing.
content.fractal_exempt: 8 nodes in linear pipeline. SensoryInput -> FeatureExtraction -> SalienceComputation -> NoveltyDetection -> GoalRelevance -> AttentionGate -> MultiModalIntegration -> OutputAssembly. All non-Start nodes have [ASSERT] entry gates.

aisop.main:
graph TD
    SensoryInput[Raw Stimulus Reception] --> FeatureExtraction[Feature Decomposition]
    FeatureExtraction --> SalienceComputation[Salience Scoring]
    SalienceComputation --> NoveltyDetection[Novelty & Familiarity Check]
    NoveltyDetection --> GoalRelevance[Goal-Directed Relevance]
    GoalRelevance --> AttentionGate[Attention Bottleneck Filter]
    AttentionGate --> MultiModalIntegration[Cross-Modal Binding]
    MultiModalIntegration --> OutputAssembly[Perception Output Assembly]

SensoryInput.step1: Receive raw stimulus. If operation='sample_environment': generate internal stimulus by sampling from working_memory_slots (mind-wandering) or producing a null-stimulus placeholder { modality: 'internal', content: 'ambient_monitoring', priority: 0.2, timestamp: now, raw_features: [] }. If operation='attention_gate': validate sensory_input is present and well-formed.
SensoryInput.step2: MODALITY CLASSIFICATION: Identify stimulus modality. For text input: modality='text'. For event triggers (timers, system signals): modality='event'. For internal generation: modality='internal'. Tag stimulus with modality metadata.
SensoryInput.step3: RAW FEATURE EXTRACTION PREP: Tokenize stimulus content into feature candidates. For text: extract key phrases, named entities, emotional markers, question indicators, topic keywords. For events: extract event_type, urgency_level, source. Compile as raw_features array: [{ feature_id, feature_type, raw_value, position }].
SensoryInput.constraints: (A) Maximum 50 raw features per stimulus to prevent processing overload. (B) Internal stimuli must be flagged as modality='internal' -- never present as external. (C) Null stimulus must still produce minimal feature set for downstream processing. WEB_SEARCH_BEST_PRACTICES (v2.2.0 B-2): When web_search or web_fetch is invoked from this module (fallback scenarios), apply: query decomposition (2-3 sub-queries), source credibility ranking, ≥2 source cross-validation, 12-month recency preference, ≤3 queries per invocation.
SensoryInput.Error: retry(2) -> circuit-breaker -> fallback(generate null-stimulus with minimal features) -> inform(User). LOW.

FeatureExtraction.step1: [ASSERT] SensoryInput executed. If false -> go back to SensoryInput. | Process raw_features into structured feature representations. For each raw feature, compute: { feature_id, feature_type: 'semantic'|'syntactic'|'emotional'|'spatial'|'temporal', value: string, embedding_proxy: float(0-1) (semantic similarity proxy), extraction_confidence: float(0-1) }.
FeatureExtraction.step2: FEATURE CLUSTERING: Group related features into feature bundles. Features with embedding_proxy similarity > 0.7 are clustered. Each cluster gets a cluster_label summarizing the grouped features. This reduces downstream processing load.
FeatureExtraction.step3: Output extracted_features: [{ feature_id, feature_type, value, embedding_proxy, extraction_confidence, cluster_id }] and feature_clusters: [{ cluster_id, cluster_label, member_count, avg_confidence }].
FeatureExtraction.constraints: (A) Feature extraction must preserve original feature ordering for positional analysis. (B) Clustering threshold 0.7 is configurable via schema.json. (C) Maximum 20 clusters to prevent fragmentation.
FeatureExtraction.Error: retry(2) -> circuit-breaker -> fallback(pass raw_features without extraction as identity transform) -> inform(User). LOW.

SalienceComputation.step1: [ASSERT] FeatureExtraction executed. If false -> go back to FeatureExtraction. | Compute salience score for each extracted feature using dual-pathway model: (a) BOTTOM-UP (stimulus-driven): salience_bottom_up = intensity * unexpectedness * emotional_charge. Intensity from feature extraction_confidence. Unexpectedness from novelty detection (next node provides, use prior estimate = 0.5 for first pass. NOVELTY FEEDBACK (v1.6.0): After NoveltyDetection completes, SalienceComputation results are retroactively updated with actual novelty scores via the adjusted_salience computation in NoveltyDetection step3. The initial 0.5 prior is a placeholder only — final salience always incorporates real novelty). Emotional_charge from emotional markers in feature_type. MOOD-CONGRUENT SALIENCE MODULATION (v2.19.0 B-1): If mood_vector param is non-null, apply affective modulation to bottom-up salience: arousal_amplification = 1.0 + 0.2 * (mood_vector.arousal - 0.5). salience_bottom_up *= clamp(arousal_amplification, 0.8, 1.2). High arousal amplifies bottom-up salience (heightened alertness), low arousal dampens it. For emotional_charge component: if mood_vector.valence > 0.3 AND feature has positive emotional markers: emotional_charge *= 1.15 (mood-congruent positive features get salience boost). If mood_vector.valence < -0.3 AND feature has negative/threat emotional markers: emotional_charge *= 1.15 (mood-congruent negative features get salience boost -- threat vigilance). This implements Niedenthal (2007) mood-congruent perception: current affective state selectively enhances processing of mood-congruent stimuli. Backward compatible: if mood_vector is null, skip modulation entirely.
SalienceComputation.step2: (b) TOP-DOWN (goal-directed): salience_top_down = goal_relevance * working_memory_priming * task_urgency. Goal_relevance computed against active_goals. Working_memory_priming = 1.0 if feature matches any working_memory_slot content, 0.5 otherwise. Task_urgency from highest-priority active goal.
SalienceComputation.step3: COMBINED SALIENCE: salience_score = 0.4 * salience_bottom_up + 0.6 * salience_top_down. The top-down bias (0.6) reflects goal-directed cognitive processing dominance in task contexts. GWT MULTI-SOURCE SIGNAL FUSION (v2.13.0 B-2): After computing base salience_score, integrate cross-module signals from global_workspace.broadcast_buffer (passed via params). For each feature in salience_map, scan broadcast_buffer for semantically related broadcast entries (semantic_similarity(feature.value, broadcast.value_summary) > 0.4). For each matching broadcast entry: compute gwt_signal_strength = broadcast.salience * recency_factor, where recency_factor = 1.0 / (1 + (current_tick - broadcast.tick_number)). Aggregate gwt_fusion_boost = sum(gwt_signal_strength for all matching broadcasts) / max(matching_count, 1). Clamp gwt_fusion_boost to [0.0, 0.25] (max 25% boost from GWT signals). Apply Bayesian fusion: fused_salience = salience_score * (1 + gwt_fusion_boost). Re-clamp to [0.0, 1.0]. SOURCE WEIGHTING (v2.13.0 B-2): Weight broadcast signals by source module credibility: reasoning broadcasts get weight 1.2 (high cognitive authority), emotion broadcasts get weight 1.0, metacognition broadcasts get weight 0.8 (advisory), compliance broadcasts get weight 0.6 (regulatory, less salience-relevant). gwt_signal_strength *= source_weight. CONFLICT RESOLUTION: If broadcast_buffer contains contradictory signals (e.g., reasoning says high-salience but emotion says low-salience for same feature), use weighted average by source credibility rather than max. Log: { event: 'gwt_fusion_applied', features_boosted: count(features where gwt_fusion_boost > 0.05), avg_gwt_boost, broadcast_entries_consumed: matching_count, tick_number }. Output salience_map: [{ feature_id, salience_score, bottom_up_component, top_down_component, gwt_fusion_boost }].
SalienceComputation.step3_4: GWT ADAPTIVE BROADCAST CYCLE FREQUENCY (v2.34.0 B-3): Adjust GWT broadcast fusion frequency based on current cognitive load. Read adaptive_broadcast_frequency config from main.aisop.json params (passed via cognitive_state or params). Extract { base_cycle_interval, high_load_multiplier, low_load_multiplier, load_threshold_high, load_threshold_low }. If adaptive_broadcast_frequency is null or absent: use defaults (base_cycle_interval=1.0, no frequency adjustment -- backward compatible). Compute current cognitive_load_level from cognitive_state (attention_load, working_memory utilization, or param). Determine effective_cycle_interval: if cognitive_load_level > load_threshold_high (default 0.7): effective_cycle_interval = base_cycle_interval * high_load_multiplier (default 0.5 -- faster cycles under high load, more frequent broadcast fusion to accelerate cross-module integration when processing demands are high). If cognitive_load_level < load_threshold_low (default 0.3): effective_cycle_interval = base_cycle_interval * low_load_multiplier (default 2.0 -- slower cycles under low load, conserving processing resources during routine operation). Otherwise (between thresholds): effective_cycle_interval = base_cycle_interval (standard frequency). FREQUENCY MODULATION: Apply effective_cycle_interval as a scaling factor to gwt_fusion_boost in step3: when effective_cycle_interval < 1.0 (high load, faster cycles), amplify gwt_fusion_boost by factor 1.0 / effective_cycle_interval (capped at 2.0x amplification). When effective_cycle_interval > 1.0 (low load, slower cycles), attenuate gwt_fusion_boost by factor 1.0 / effective_cycle_interval (minimum 0.5x attenuation). This implements the principle that under high cognitive load, cross-module broadcast signals should be weighted more heavily to facilitate rapid information sharing, while under low load, reduced broadcast emphasis allows more focused bottom-up/top-down processing. Log: { event: 'adaptive_broadcast_frequency', cognitive_load_level: float, effective_cycle_interval: float, fusion_boost_modifier: float, load_zone: 'high'|'normal'|'low', tick_number }.
SalienceComputation.step3_5: UNIFIED BROADCAST WEIGHTING INTERFACE (v2.27.0 B-2): SalienceComputation and MultiModalIntegration both apply GWT broadcast priority weighting. As of v2.27.0, both nodes consume the unified broadcast_weighting_interface defined in main.aisop.json params, which consolidates GWT broadcast priority logic into a single configurable interface. SalienceComputation applies the interface for salience-level fusion (step3 gwt_fusion_boost), while MultiModalIntegration applies it for integration-level fusion (step2_5 weighted_broadcast_influence). Both read from the same broadcast_priority_weights and broadcast_consumer_weights params, ensuring consistent cross-module weighting without configuration divergence. GWT BROADCAST PRIORITY WEIGHTING (v2.15.0 B-2, v2.27.0 B-2 unified): After GWT multi-source signal fusion in step3, apply broadcast_consumer_weights from cognitive_state to re-weight broadcast contributions per source module. (1) READ WEIGHTS: Load broadcast_consumer_weights from cognitive_state (passed via params). Format: { module_name: weight_float } e.g. { "reasoning": 1.3, "emotion": 0.9, "metacognition": 1.0, "compliance": 0.7 }. If broadcast_consumer_weights is absent, null, or empty: fall back to uniform weight 1.0 for all modules (backward compatible -- no behavior change from v2.14.0). (2) APPLY WEIGHTS: For each broadcast_buffer entry consumed in step3's GWT fusion, look up source module in broadcast_consumer_weights. Multiply the gwt_signal_strength by the consumer weight: weighted_gwt_signal = gwt_signal_strength * broadcast_consumer_weights.get(source_module, 1.0). Clamp individual consumer weights to [0.0, 2.0] before application. (3) RECOMPUTE FUSION: Recompute gwt_fusion_boost using weighted signals: gwt_fusion_boost = sum(weighted_gwt_signal for all matching broadcasts) / max(matching_count, 1). Re-clamp gwt_fusion_boost to [0.0, 0.25]. Recompute fused_salience = salience_score * (1 + gwt_fusion_boost). Re-clamp to [0.0, 1.0]. Update salience_map entries with recomputed values. (4) LOG: { event: "gwt_broadcast_priority_weighting_applied", consumer_weights_source: "cognitive_state" | "uniform_fallback", weights_used: broadcast_consumer_weights or { "all": 1.0 }, entries_reweighted: count, avg_weighted_boost: float, delta_from_unweighted: float, tick_number }. Note: This step supplements (not replaces) the static SOURCE WEIGHTING in step3 -- step3's credibility weights establish a baseline, and step3_5's consumer weights provide runtime-configurable overlay. The effective weight for a broadcast entry is: step3_source_weight * step3_5_consumer_weight.
SalienceComputation.step3_6: COGITATE DUAL-PATHWAY IGNITION MODEL (v2.34.0 B-5, replaces v2.31.0 B-2 single-pathway adaptation): Based on COGITATE 2025 adversarial collaboration findings and Nature multimodal results showing GWT sustained activity partially supported in prefrontal but not posterior cortex, replace the single adaptive_ignition_threshold with a dual-pathway computation modeling content-specific posterior pathway and access-specific prefrontal pathway. (1) POSTERIOR PATHWAY (content-specific): Computes content_ignition_threshold based on feature content characteristics and sensory processing. content_ignition_threshold = base_threshold * content_modulator, where base_threshold = gwt_ignition_threshold param from main.aisop.json (default 0.4, range [0.1, 0.9]) and content_modulator = 1.0 + 0.25 * feature_specificity - 0.15 * emotional_charge, where feature_specificity = mean(extraction_confidence for features in salience_map) (higher specificity = clearer content = higher threshold -- well-defined content needs less cross-module integration), emotional_charge = mean(emotional markers intensity for features in salience_map) (higher emotional charge = lower threshold -- emotional content triggers easier ignition per affective priority). Clamp content_ignition_threshold to [0.20, 0.55]. COGITATE finding: posterior pathway does NOT show sustained ignition at offset -- this pathway is transient and content-locked. (2) PREFRONTAL PATHWAY (access-specific): Computes access_ignition_threshold based on cognitive access demands and executive control state. access_ignition_threshold = base_threshold * access_modulator, where access_modulator = 1.0 - 0.3 * attention_load + 0.2 * (1.0 - mean_prediction_error), where attention_load = current attention_load from AttentionGate (higher load = lower threshold -- more competition needs easier access to workspace for conflict resolution), mean_prediction_error = from predictive coding in AttentionGate.step4 (lower prediction error = higher threshold -- predictable environment needs less prefrontal access). Clamp access_ignition_threshold to [0.25, 0.65]. COGITATE finding: prefrontal pathway DOES show partial sustained activity -- this pathway supports extended workspace access for features under active executive processing. (3) DUAL-PATHWAY FUSION: Compute adaptive_ignition_threshold = min(content_ignition_threshold, access_ignition_threshold) * 0.8 + max(content_ignition_threshold, access_ignition_threshold) * 0.2. This weighted-min fusion ensures that if EITHER pathway supports ignition (low threshold), the feature can access the global workspace, consistent with COGITATE's finding that content and access pathways are partially independent. Clamp final adaptive_ignition_threshold to [0.25, 0.6]. (4) OFFSET IGNITION SUPPRESSION (retained from v2.31.0): COGITATE found ignition does NOT reliably occur at stimulus offset. When a feature was present in previous tick but absent in current tick (stimulus_offset_detected = true): suppress GWT fusion for that feature (set gwt_fusion_boost = 0 for offset features). Apply offset suppression ONLY to posterior-pathway ignition; prefrontal pathway may still maintain access for offset features under active executive processing (sustained prefrontal activity). (5) SUSTAINED IGNITION PREFERENCE (updated for dual-pathway): For features present in attention_buffer for 3+ consecutive ticks with stable salience (variance < 0.1): apply sustained_ignition_bonus = 0.12 to gwt_fusion_boost (increased from 0.1 to reflect prefrontal sustained activity support). For features present 5+ consecutive ticks: apply enhanced_sustained_bonus = 0.18 (deep executive engagement). (6) PATHWAY DIAGNOSTICS: Record dual_pathway_metrics = { content_ignition_threshold, access_ignition_threshold, fusion_threshold: adaptive_ignition_threshold, pathway_dominant: content_ignition_threshold < access_ignition_threshold ? 'posterior' : 'prefrontal', content_modulator, access_modulator, feature_specificity, emotional_charge_avg }. (7) LOG: { event: 'cogitate_dual_pathway_ignition', content_threshold: float, access_threshold: float, fused_threshold: float, pathway_dominant: string, offset_features_suppressed: int, sustained_features_boosted: int, tick_number }. Backward compatible: if attention_buffer is empty (first tick), use gwt_ignition_threshold param value (default 0.4). If gwt_ignition_threshold param is absent, fall back to hardcoded 0.4.
SalienceComputation.step3_7: GWT BROADCAST CYCLE TIMING METRICS (v2.32.0 B-2): After COGITATE ignition adaptation, compute observable timing metrics for GWT broadcast cycle performance. (1) BROADCAST DURATION: Measure broadcast_duration_ms = time elapsed from first feature entering GWT fusion (step3 start) to final fused_salience computation complete (step3_6 end). Since LLM-native processing does not have real-time clocks, estimate broadcast_duration_ms = feature_count * avg_fusion_complexity * base_latency_factor, where avg_fusion_complexity = mean(matching_broadcast_entries per feature), base_latency_factor = 2.5ms (calibrated constant). Clamp to [1.0, 500.0]ms. (2) IGNITION LATENCY: ignition_latency_ms = time from stimulus onset (SensoryInput step1) to first feature exceeding adaptive_ignition_threshold in GWT fusion. Estimate as: ignition_latency_ms = steps_before_first_ignition * 3.0ms, where steps_before_first_ignition = index of first feature in salience_map with gwt_fusion_boost > 0.05. If no feature achieves ignition: ignition_latency_ms = null (no ignition this tick). (3) ACCESS COMPETITION: access_competition_count = count of broadcast_buffer entries that competed for the same feature's attention (entries with semantic_similarity > adaptive_ignition_threshold for the same feature_id). Higher competition indicates richer workspace dynamics. (4) OUTPUT: Append gwt_timing_metrics to SalienceComputation output: { broadcast_duration_ms: float, ignition_latency_ms: float|null, access_competition_count: int, features_ignited: int (count of features with gwt_fusion_boost > 0.05), broadcast_efficiency: features_ignited / max(feature_count, 1), tick_number }. (5) LOG: { event: 'gwt_broadcast_timing', broadcast_duration_ms, ignition_latency_ms, access_competition_count, features_ignited, broadcast_efficiency, tick_number }. Backward compatible: if broadcast_buffer is empty (no GWT fusion occurred), gwt_timing_metrics = { broadcast_duration_ms: 0, ignition_latency_ms: null, access_competition_count: 0, features_ignited: 0, broadcast_efficiency: 0, tick_number }.
SalienceComputation.constraints: (A) Salience scores clamp to [0.0, 1.0]. (B) Top-down/bottom-up weights (0.6/0.4) are configurable via schema.json. (C) Features with no goal relevance still get minimum bottom-up salience. (D) broadcast_consumer_weights values clamp to [0.0, 2.0]; absent weights default to 1.0 (uniform fallback). (E) When broadcast_consumer_weights is not provided, behavior is identical to v2.14.0 (backward compatible). (F) COGITATE ignition adaptation (v2.31.0 B-2): adaptive_ignition_threshold clamped to [0.25, 0.6]; offset suppression applies only to features with stimulus_offset_detected=true; sustained bonus requires 3+ consecutive tick presence. (G) GWT broadcast timing metrics (v2.32.0 B-2): broadcast_duration_ms clamped to [1.0, 500.0]ms; ignition_latency_ms null when no ignition; access_competition_count is non-negative integer.
SalienceComputation.Error: retry(2) -> circuit-breaker -> fallback(assign uniform salience 0.5 to all features) -> inform(User). LOW.

NoveltyDetection.step1: [ASSERT] SalienceComputation executed. If false -> go back to SalienceComputation. | Read schema.json from memory_dir via file_system. Extract known_concepts and familiarity_baseline. For each feature, compute novelty_score: compare feature value against known_concepts. If no match: novelty=1.0 (completely novel). If exact match: novelty=0.0 (completely familiar). Partial match: novelty = 1.0 - similarity_score.
NoveltyDetection.step1_5: TRUST-AWARE RETRIEVAL (v2.36.0 B3, memory-poisoning hardening; baseline H-2, ref arXiv 2601.05504 MINJA-defense / arXiv 2510.02373 A-MemGuard): When matching features against schema.json known_concepts/long_term_entries, apply a deterministic, auditable trust filter at the RETRIEVAL stage (paired with the append-stage trust scoring in consolidation.StrengthEvaluation, so trust is enforced at BOTH ends of the memory pipeline). (1) EFFECTIVE TRUST: for each retrieved entry, effective_trust = base_trust * temporal_decay, where base_trust = entry.trust_score (default 0.7 for legacy/untagged entries) and temporal_decay is computed from the EXISTING {memory_dir}/decay_config.json constants (base_decay_rate=0.05, type_specific_decay per entry.type, minimum_strength=0.1) -- REUSE decay_config.json as the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH; do NOT introduce a parallel decay constant. (2) QUARANTINE: entries with effective_trust < 0.2 OR entry.quarantined==true are EXCLUDED from novelty matching (they neither lower novelty nor get surfaced); they are not deleted here (read-only on schema), only filtered. Older poisoned entries thus lose trust over time and self-heal out of retrieval (ASR decreases over benign queries). (3) DETERMINISTIC: trust scoring MUST be deterministic given the same inputs (no LLM-only judgement) so it is auditable. (4) MEMORY-OP AUDIT: append one audit record per retrieval pass to {memory_dir}/memory_audit_log.json via file_system (append-only; atomic .tmp+rename; max 500 entries FIFO; each record { schema_version: '1.0', ts, module: 'perception', op: 'retrieve', entries_considered, entries_quarantined, min_effective_trust, tick_number }). Since perception declares file_system read_only, EMIT perception_output.memory_audit_pending = the audit record for the main module's memory-write authority to flush (same write-back pattern as attention_stats_update), so the read_only contract is preserved. Log: { event: 'trust_aware_retrieval', entries_quarantined: count, single_source_of_truth: 'memory/decay_config.json' }.
NoveltyDetection.step2: HABITUATION CHECK: Compare current features against attention_buffer (recent history). Features that appeared in the last 3 attention cycles get habituation_penalty: novelty_score *= 0.5 (diminishing returns on repeated stimuli). This models sensory adaptation.
NoveltyDetection.step3: Update salience_map: for each feature, adjust salience_score by novelty bonus: adjusted_salience = salience_score + 0.2 * novelty_score. Re-clamp to [0.0, 1.0]. SCHEMA GROWTH CONTROL (v2.25.0 B-6): Before flagging high-novelty features for schema update, check schema size. Read schema_entry_count from {memory_dir}/schema.json via file_system (count top-level entries in 'entries' array, or count keys if object format). If schema_entry_count > 500: elevate novelty threshold for schema update requests from 0.8 to 0.9. Only flag features with novelty_score > elevated_threshold for potential schema update. Log: { event: 'schema_growth_control_active', schema_entry_count: int, base_threshold: 0.8, elevated_threshold: 0.9, features_above_elevated: count, tick_number }. If schema_entry_count <= 500: use standard threshold 0.8. Flag high-novelty features (novelty > threshold) for potential schema update during consolidation.
NoveltyDetection.constraints: (A) Novelty detection must not modify schema.json -- read-only operation. (B) Habituation penalty applies only to features seen in last 3 cycles, not all history. (C) Novel features are flagged but not automatically stored.
NoveltyDetection.Error: retry(2) -> circuit-breaker -> fallback(skip novelty adjustment, use original salience_map) -> inform(User). LOW.

GoalRelevance.step1: [ASSERT] NoveltyDetection executed. If false -> go back to NoveltyDetection. | For each feature in salience_map, compute fine-grained goal relevance against each active goal. For each goal in active_goals: relevance = semantic_similarity(feature.value, goal.description) * goal.priority. Feature's overall goal_relevance = max(relevance across all goals).
GoalRelevance.step2: GOAL-CONFLICT DETECTION: If a feature is relevant to multiple competing goals (relevance > 0.6 for 2+ goals), flag as conflict_feature. Attach conflict metadata: { competing_goals: [goal_ids], conflict_type: 'resource'|'priority'|'temporal' }. These conflict features receive a salience boost (+0.15) because conflicts demand cognitive attention.
GoalRelevance.step3: Update salience_map with refined goal_relevance scores. Sort features by final adjusted_salience (descending). Output ranked_features and any conflict_features for downstream processing.
GoalRelevance.constraints: (A) Goal relevance must reference actual active_goals, not hallucinated goals. (B) Conflict detection requires relevance > 0.6 threshold. (C) Maximum 3 conflict features per cycle to prevent attention fragmentation.
GoalRelevance.Error: retry(2) -> circuit-breaker -> fallback(use salience_map without goal refinement) -> inform(User). LOW.

AttentionGate.step1: [ASSERT] GoalRelevance executed. If false -> go back to GoalRelevance. | Apply attention bottleneck filter. Set attention_threshold = 0.3 (configurable). THRESHOLD MICRO-ADJUSTMENT (v2.11.0 B-5): Before applying the threshold, load historical attention performance from {memory_dir}/attention_stats.json via file_system (create with defaults if not present: { false_positive_count: 0, false_negative_count: 0, total_gate_decisions: 0, threshold_adjustment: 0.0 }). Compute false_positive_rate = false_positive_count / max(total_gate_decisions, 1) (features that passed gate but were not useful in downstream reasoning/decision). Compute false_negative_rate = false_negative_count / max(total_gate_decisions, 1) (features suppressed by gate that were later needed, detected via triage_miss anomalies from metacognition). Apply micro-adjustment: if false_positive_rate > 0.3: increase threshold by +0.01 (be more selective). If false_negative_rate > 0.2: decrease threshold by -0.01 (be more permissive). Clamp threshold_adjustment to [-0.05, +0.05] (maximum 0.05 deviation from base threshold). Effective attention_threshold = base_threshold + threshold_adjustment. Clamp effective attention_threshold to [0.2, 0.5] (never too permissive or too restrictive). WRITE-PATH CLARIFICATION (v2.11.0 B-5): Since perception module declares file_system as read_only, attention_stats updates are computed in-module but returned to the caller via perception_output.attention_stats_update = { false_positive_count, false_negative_count, total_gate_decisions, threshold_adjustment }. The main module's Attention.step2 is responsible for writing attention_stats_update to {memory_dir}/attention_stats.json via its own file_system (read_only:false). This follows the same pattern as emotion module's emotion_inertia_update (v1.7.0 QI-6 fix). Log { event: 'attention_threshold_adjusted', base: 0.3, adjustment: threshold_adjustment, effective: attention_threshold, fp_rate: false_positive_rate, fn_rate: false_negative_rate } when adjustment != 0. THRESHOLD CONVERGENCE DETECTOR (v2.12.0 B-6): Track adjustment history for convergence detection. If abs(adjustment) < 0.001 for 100 consecutive ticks (from attention_stats.adjustment_history), set threshold_converged = true and STOP micro-adjustments (save compute). If environment change detected (attention_gate_threshold_learning enabled AND significant stimulus distribution shift: abs(mean_salience_current - mean_salience_baseline) > 0.2), set threshold_converged = false and RESTART learning (threshold_reset_trigger = true). Log: { event: 'threshold_convergence', converged: bool, consecutive_small_adjustments: N, trigger: 'stability' | 'environment_change' }. Features with adjusted_salience >= attention_threshold pass the gate (gate_passed=true). Features below threshold are suppressed (gate_passed=false).
AttentionGate.step2: CAPACITY LIMIT: From passed features, select top K (default K=5) by salience score. These become attended_features. Remaining passed features go to suppressed_but_available pool (accessible if primary attended features are insufficient). Compute attention_load = len(attended_features) / K. CONVERGENCE_LOCK (v2.22.0 B-1): if attention_threshold oscillation amplitude < 0.01 for 5 consecutive ticks, lock threshold to current value (prevent wasteful micro-adjustment). Record convergence_locked=true in perception_output. Unlock on novelty spike (novelty_score > 0.8).
AttentionGate.step2_5: CONVERGENCE_RATE_CONTROL (v2.28.0 B-4): Add adaptive convergence rate parameter to convergence_lock mechanism. Compute convergence_rate = base_rate * (1 - cognitive_load_level). base_rate default = 0.1 (from params or context). Under high cognitive load (>0.7): convergence_rate decreases, slowing threshold adjustment to prevent over-filtering when processing capacity is strained. Under low cognitive load (<0.3): convergence_rate increases, allowing faster threshold adaptation for efficient attention allocation. Bounds: convergence_rate is clamped to [0.02, 0.2]. If convergence_lock is active (threshold stable for >= 3 ticks): reduce rate by 50% to maintain stability (convergence_rate *= 0.5, then re-clamp). Write convergence_rate to attention_stats alongside existing threshold tracking: perception_output.attention_stats_update.convergence_rate = convergence_rate. Log: { event: 'convergence_rate_control', base_rate: 0.1, cognitive_load_level: float, convergence_rate: float, convergence_lock_active: bool, rate_halved: bool, tick_number }.
AttentionGate.step2_7: ADAPTIVE ATTENTION CHUNKING (v2.31.0 B-5): Under high cognitive load, automatically chunk low-priority attended features to conserve processing capacity. (1) CHUNKING TRIGGER: If cognitive_load_level > 0.7 (from params/cognitive_state) AND len(attended_features) >= 4: activate chunking. (2) CHUNK FORMATION: Group attended_features[2:] (all except top-2 by salience) into semantic clusters using pairwise similarity. Features with semantic_similarity > 0.6 form a chunk. Each chunk is represented by a single composite feature: { feature_id: "chunk_{chunk_index}", value: merged_summary_of_chunk_features, salience_score: max(chunk_member_saliences), chunk_members: [original_feature_ids], chunk_size: N }. (3) CAPACITY RECOVERY: After chunking, effective attention slot usage = 2 (preserved top features) + num_chunks (instead of original feature count). This frees processing capacity without losing information entirely. (4) DECHUNKING: If a chunk receives downstream attention (e.g., decision module queries a chunk member), dechunk on demand: expand chunk back to individual features for detailed processing. Set dechunked = true in output. (5) METRICS: Record chunking_report = { chunking_triggered: bool, cognitive_load_at_trigger: float, features_before: int, chunks_formed: int, features_after: int (top-2 + chunks), capacity_recovery_pct: float }. If cognitive_load_level <= 0.7: skip chunking entirely (no overhead for normal operation). Log: { event: "adaptive_chunking", triggered: bool, chunks_formed: int, capacity_recovered_pct: float, tick_number }.
AttentionGate.step2_8: ATTENTION DECAY-CONVERGENCE COUPLING (v2.32.0 B-4): When salience convergence is detected among attended features, reduce attention decay rate to maintain focused attention on converging stimuli. (1) CONVERGENCE DETECTION: Compute salience_std = standard_deviation(attended_features[*].salience_score). Define convergence_threshold = 0.08 (configurable). If salience_std < convergence_threshold (salience scores are clustering tightly — features have similar priority): salience_convergence_detected = true. (2) DECAY RATE COUPLING: When salience_convergence_detected = true: reduce attention_decay_rate by 50% for this tick: coupled_decay_rate = attention_decay_rate * 0.5. Rationale: when multiple features converge on similar salience, the cognitive system is in a state of balanced attention — reducing decay preserves this distributed focus state rather than allowing stochastic decay to arbitrarily drop one converging feature. (3) ANTI-STAGNATION GUARD: If salience_convergence_detected persists for 5+ consecutive ticks (tracked via convergence_streak counter in attention_stats): gradually restore decay rate — coupled_decay_rate = attention_decay_rate * (0.5 + 0.1 * (convergence_streak - 5)). Clamp coupled_decay_rate to [attention_decay_rate * 0.5, attention_decay_rate * 1.0]. At convergence_streak >= 10: fully restore original decay rate (prevent permanent decay suppression). (4) APPLY: Use coupled_decay_rate (instead of attention_decay_rate) for all attention buffer maintenance this tick. Pass coupled_decay_rate in perception_output.attention_stats_update.coupled_decay_rate for main module consumption. (5) METRICS: Record decay_convergence_coupling = { convergence_detected: bool, salience_std: float, convergence_threshold: float, coupled_decay_rate: float, original_decay_rate: float, decay_reduction_pct: float, convergence_streak: int }. Log: { event: 'decay_convergence_coupling', convergence_detected: bool, salience_std, coupled_decay_rate, convergence_streak, tick_number }. Backward compatible: if salience_std >= convergence_threshold, no coupling applied (coupled_decay_rate = attention_decay_rate).
AttentionGate.step3: ATTENTION FOCUS: Identify primary attention_focus as the highest-salience attended feature. If attention_focus is a conflict_feature, note conflict_active=true for downstream decision module awareness. Output attention_result: { attended_features, attention_focus, suppressed_features, attention_load, conflict_active, chunking_report (v2.31.0 B-5), decay_convergence_coupling (v2.32.0 B-4) }.
AttentionGate.step4: PREDICTION ERROR SIGNAL (v1.3.0): Implement lightweight predictive coding within perception. (1) PREDICTION GENERATION: Based on attention_buffer (recent stimuli) and working_memory context, generate predicted_features: expected sensory features for the current tick. Use simple pattern: predicted_features = weighted_average(attention_buffer[-3:].raw_features) with exponential recency weighting (weights: 0.5, 0.3, 0.2). If attention_buffer has fewer than 3 entries, use available entries with uniform weights. (2) PREDICTION ERROR COMPUTATION: For each actual raw_feature in sensory_input.raw_features, compute prediction_error = 1.0 - max_similarity(feature, predicted_features). Aggregate: mean_prediction_error = mean(all prediction_errors). (3) SURPRISE SIGNAL: If mean_prediction_error > 0.7 (highly unexpected input): boost all salience_scores by surprise_boost = mean_prediction_error * 0.3 (surprising stimuli get more attention). Set prediction_surprise_flag = true in attention_result. (4) HABITUATION: If mean_prediction_error < 0.2 (highly expected input): apply habituation_dampening = 0.8 to all salience_scores (reduce attention to predictable stimuli unless goal-relevant). Goal-relevant features (salience from goal-relevance > 0.5) are exempt from habituation dampening. (5) Record prediction_error_report: { mean_prediction_error, surprise_flag, habituation_applied, predicted_features_count, actual_features_count } in attention_result for downstream consumption by MetaCognition. Backward compatible: if attention_buffer is empty (first tick), skip prediction and proceed with standard salience computation.
AttentionGate.step4_5: PREDICTION ERROR BOUNDS (v1.5.0): Clamp prediction_error to range [0.0, 1.0] (prediction error is always non-negative by construction: 1.0 - max_similarity produces [0.0, 1.0]): prediction_error = clamp(raw_prediction_error, 0.0, 1.0). If raw value exceeds bounds, set prediction_error_clamped = true in output and log the raw value for debugging. This prevents extreme prediction errors from destabilizing attention allocation and novelty scoring.
AttentionGate.step4_6: ENTROPY-BASED EXPLORATION DETECTION (v1.6.0): After attention gating, compute attention_entropy = -sum(p_i * log2(p_i)) over normalized salience distribution of attended_features, where p_i = feature_salience / sum(all_salience). If all salience equal: attention_entropy = log2(n_features) (maximum entropy). Normalize: normalized_entropy = attention_entropy / log2(max(n_features, 2)). If normalized_entropy > 0.8: system is in exploration state (diffuse attention, no clear focus). Set exploration_mode = true in attention_result. If normalized_entropy < 0.3: system is in exploitation state (focused attention). Set exploration_mode = false. Between 0.3-0.8: transitional. Pass exploration_mode to metacognition for MSI integration.
AttentionGate.constraints: (A) Attention threshold 0.3 is a hard minimum -- never pass features below this. (B) K=5 default capacity is configurable via schema.json. (C) At least 1 feature must pass even if all below threshold -- select highest salience as minimum. (D) Prediction error signal (v1.3.0) is backward compatible: skipped when attention_buffer is empty. (E) Surprise boost and habituation dampening are applied after initial attention gating and re-clamped to [0.0, 1.0].
AttentionGate.Error: retry(2) -> circuit-breaker -> fallback(pass top 3 features by raw salience without full gating) -> inform(User). MEDIUM.

MultiModalIntegration.step1: [ASSERT] AttentionGate executed. If false -> go back to AttentionGate. | Bind attended features across modalities. Group attended_features by modality (text, event, internal). For multi-modal stimuli, compute cross-modal binding: features from different modalities that refer to the same entity or event are linked into integrated_percepts.
MultiModalIntegration.step2: TEMPORAL BINDING: Check temporal proximity of features. Features within the same stimulus timestamp are temporally bound. Features from attention_buffer (previous cycles) that are within 3-cycle window are checked for temporal continuity -- continuing percepts get continuity_bonus to activation.
MultiModalIntegration.step2_5: GWT BROADCAST PRIORITY WEIGHTING (v2.14.0 B-1, v2.27.0 B-2 unified): Apply broadcast_priority_weights from the unified broadcast_weighting_interface (main.aisop.json params) to modulate cross-module broadcast signal integration. This node shares the broadcast_weighting_interface with SalienceComputation.step3_5, ensuring consistent priority weighting across both perception processing stages. For each broadcast_buffer entry, look up source module weight from broadcast_priority_weights (default 1.0 if module not listed). Multiply gwt_signal_strength by source_weight from broadcast_priority_weights instead of the fixed credibility weights in SalienceComputation. This replaces the static source weighting (reasoning=1.2, emotion=1.0, metacognition=0.8, compliance=0.6) with configurable runtime weights. Integration formula: weighted_broadcast_influence = sum(broadcast_entry.salience * broadcast_priority_weights[source_module] * recency_factor) / max(entry_count, 1). Apply weighted_broadcast_influence as integration_boost to cross-modal binding strength: integration_strength *= (1 + clamp(weighted_broadcast_influence, 0.0, 0.3)). Log: { event: 'gwt_priority_weighting_applied', weights_used: broadcast_priority_weights, entries_weighted: entry_count, avg_weighted_influence: float, tick_number }.
MultiModalIntegration.step2_7: CROSS-MODAL CONSISTENCY DETECTION (v2.30.0 B-4): After binding features across modalities, verify consistency of integrated percepts. For each integrated_percept with modalities.length >= 2: (1) SEMANTIC CONSISTENCY: Compare semantic content across bound features from different modalities. Compute cross_modal_agreement = proportion of feature pairs where semantic_similarity > 0.6 (features agree on entity identity/properties). If cross_modal_agreement < 0.4: flag percept as inconsistent, set consistency_flag = 'cross_modal_conflict'. (2) TEMPORAL CONSISTENCY: Verify bound features have compatible temporal signatures. If any two bound features have temporal_gap > 2 cycles AND no continuity_bonus was applied: flag temporal_inconsistency = true. (3) INTENSITY CONSISTENCY: Compare salience/activation levels across modalities for same percept. Compute intensity_variance = variance(feature.salience for feature in bound_features). If intensity_variance > 0.25: flag intensity_mismatch = true (one modality reporting much stronger signal than others — may indicate spurious binding). (4) CONSISTENCY SCORE: For each integrated percept: consistency_score = (0.5 * cross_modal_agreement + 0.3 * (1 - temporal_inconsistency) + 0.2 * (1 - clamp(intensity_variance / 0.5, 0, 1))). If consistency_score < 0.5: downgrade integration_strength by 30% (integration_strength *= 0.7), add to percept: { consistency_alert: true, consistency_score, conflict_type: 'semantic'|'temporal'|'intensity'|'multiple' }. If consistency_score < 0.3: unbind the percept entirely (treat features as independent — binding was likely spurious). (5) OUTPUT: Append consistency_report to perception output: { percepts_checked: int, inconsistencies_found: int, unbound_count: int, mean_consistency_score: float }. Flag for metacognitive review if inconsistencies_found > 2 in single cycle. Log: { event: 'cross_modal_consistency_check', percepts_checked, inconsistencies_found, mean_consistency, tick_number }.
MultiModalIntegration.step3: Output integrated_percepts: [{ percept_id, bound_features: [feature_ids], modalities: [string], temporal_span, integration_strength: float(0-1), gwt_boost_applied: float, consistency_score: float(0-1), consistency_alert: bool }]. These represent the unified perceptual objects that enter working memory.
MultiModalIntegration.constraints: (A) Cross-modal binding requires shared entity reference, not just temporal proximity. (B) Maximum 5 integrated percepts per cycle. (C) Integration strength must be >= 0.4 for a valid binding. (D) broadcast_priority_weights values clamp to [0.0, 2.0]; missing modules default to 1.0. (E) Cross-modal consistency check is mandatory for multi-modal percepts (modalities >= 2); percepts with consistency_score < 0.3 are automatically unbound (v2.30.0 B-4).
MultiModalIntegration.Error: retry(2) -> circuit-breaker -> fallback(treat each feature as independent percept without integration) -> inform(User). LOW.

OutputAssembly.step1: [ASSERT] MultiModalIntegration executed. If false -> go back to MultiModalIntegration. | Compile final perception output based on operation type. For 'sample_environment': output sensory_input structure from internally generated stimulus. For 'attention_gate': output full attention_result with integrated percepts.
OutputAssembly.step2: FORMAT OUTPUT: Assemble perception_output: { sensory_input (if sample_environment), attention_result: { attended_features, attention_focus, suppressed_features, attention_load, conflict_active }, integrated_percepts, novelty_flags: [features with novelty > 0.8], salience_summary: { mean_salience, max_salience, feature_count }, operation_completed: operation }.
OutputAssembly.step3: QUALITY CHECK: Verify output is well-formed. All required fields present. Salience scores in valid range. Feature counts consistent. If any inconsistency detected, log warning but still return output (best-effort). Return perception_output to main.aisop.json caller.
OutputAssembly.constraints: (A) Output must be complete -- no partial results. (B) Operation type must match input operation. (C) All numeric fields must be within defined ranges.
OutputAssembly.Error: retry(1) -> circuit-breaker -> fallback(return minimal output with attention_focus only) -> inform(User). LOW.
